scripts.build: npm run fetch-components && npm run build:css
scripts.verify:routes: mkdir -p ${PARITY_OUT:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/trinket-parity} && NODE_ENV=test NODE_CONFIG='{"db":{"redis":{"enabled":false}}}' node test/parity/manifest.js --out ${PARITY_OUT:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/trinket-parity}/route-manifest.json >/dev/null && if [ -n "$BASELINE_MANIFEST" ]; then node test/parity/manifest.js --compare "$BASELINE_MANIFEST" ${PARITY_OUT:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/trinket-parity}/route-manifest.json; elif [ -n "$BASELINE_APP" ]; then NODE_ENV=test NODE_CONFIG='{"db":{"redis":{"enabled":false}}}' node test/parity/manifest.js --app "$BASELINE_APP" --out ${PARITY_OUT:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/trinket-parity}/route-manifest.baseline.json >/dev/null && node test/parity/manifest.js --compare ${PARITY_OUT:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/trinket-parity}/route-manifest.baseline.json ${PARITY_OUT:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/trinket-parity}/route-manifest.json; else echo 'verify:routes: the target manifest was generated, but the comparison AAP 0.9.1 defines needs a baseline. Set BASELINE_APP to a worktree at 2f8712a that has its own node_modules (git worktree add <dir> 2f8712a && cd <dir> && npm ci), or BASELINE_MANIFEST to a manifest generated from one. The two trees cannot share node_modules, so a bare worktree is not enough.' >&2; exit 1; fi
scripts.verify:corpus: OUT=${PARITY_OUT:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/trinket-parity}; mkdir -p "$OUT" || exit 1; if [ ! -f "$OUT/route-manifest.json" ]; then npm run --silent verify:routes || exit 1; fi; if [ ! -f "$OUT/worker-result.json" ]; then npm run --silent verify:worker || exit 1; fi; node test/parity/replay.js --app . --corpus test/parity/corpus.json --annotations test/parity/corpus.json --pass both --manifest "$OUT/route-manifest.json" --worker-evidence "$OUT/worker-result.json" --node-flags "--pending-deprecation --trace-deprecation" --out "$OUT/replay-result.json" --report "$OUT/replay-report.txt" --port ${PARITY_PORT:-3010} ${PARITY_ATTEST:+--attest}
scripts.verify:joi: OUT=${PARITY_OUT:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/trinket-parity}; mkdir -p "$OUT" || exit 1; rm -f "$OUT"/joi-comparison.json*; node -e 'var f=require("fs"),o=JSON.parse(f.readFileSync("test/parity/server-overlay.json","utf8"));delete o.features;f.writeFileSync(process.argv[1],JSON.stringify(o,null,2))' "$OUT/server-overlay.as-joi-recorded.json" || exit 1; node test/parity/joi-matrix.js --compare test/parity/joi-baseline.json --overlay "$OUT/server-overlay.as-joi-recorded.json" --out "$OUT/joi-comparison.json" --port ${PARITY_PORT:-3010}
scripts.verify:worker: echo "verify:worker precondition: a Redis that answers PING at ${PARITY_REDIS:-127.0.0.1:6379} (override with PARITY_REDIS=host:port); the run isolates itself with a per-run Bull key prefix and obliterates that namespace on exit, so a shared Redis is supported" >&2 && mkdir -p ${PARITY_OUT:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/trinket-parity} && node test/parity/worker.js --redis ${PARITY_REDIS:-127.0.0.1:6379} --out ${PARITY_OUT:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/trinket-parity}/worker-result.json && node test/parity/worker.js --verify ${PARITY_OUT:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/trinket-parity}/worker-result.json
scripts.verify:parity: rc=0; for gate in routes joi storage worker corpus; do echo "== verify:$gate =="; npm run --silent verify:$gate || rc=1; done; if [ "$rc" -ne 0 ]; then echo "verify:parity FAILED - at least one gate above did not pass"; fi; exit "$rc"
